title: PromptDialog
wrapsNative: alert(_:isPresented:actions:message:) with a TextField in its actions
summary: Asking for one short value is the system alert with a TextField among its actions. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: To ask for a single short value without leaving the screen: a name for a saved view, a new name for a group, a link address.
whenNotToUse: Not when the value must be checked before the dialog closes, is more than one line, or is saved while the dialog shows progress: the alert closes on any button. Use a sheet with MonarchTextField for those, as in the second example.
api: func alert<A: View, M: View>(_ title: String, isPresented: Binding<Bool>, actions: () -> A, message: () -> M) -> some View
Button(_ title: String, role: ButtonRole?, action: () -> Void)

states.name: presented
states.description: The system alert with the title, the message, the field and the buttons. The keyboard opens with the field focused.

states.name: dismissed
states.description: Any button closes the alert. The cancel role also answers the escape gesture.

appearance: The alert is drawn by the system in every theme. Monarch colours, type and the Monarch text field are not applied inside it; only TextField and SecureField are shown, other views are ignored.
platformNotes: The web PromptDialog validates (required, maxLength, url and email types, a validate function), shows an error under the field, keeps the dialog open while an async save is pending, has a multiline mode, and offers usePrompt, which returns a promise. The system alert has none of these: it closes when a button is tapped, so check the value afterwards or use a sheet with MonarchTextField, which shows helper and error text. The web's inputType maps to keyboardType, textContentType and textInputAutocapitalization on the TextField. A promise-style call is a withCheckedContinuation around the same state. Android uses AlertDialog with an OutlinedTextField in the same way.
accessibility: System behaviour: the alert confines VoiceOver and keyboard focus, reads the title and message when it appears, and returns focus when it closes.
The TextField title is the placeholder and the spoken name of the field; write it as a label ("Name"), not as an example value.
The button with the cancel role answers the escape gesture.
The alert follows Dynamic Type and scrolls when the message is long.
edgeCases: The text binding keeps its value after the alert closes; reset it before presenting again.
Do not rely on disabling the Save button while the field is empty; treat an empty value as cancel in the action, as the example does.
A second TextField or a SecureField can be added for a name and password; more than two fields belong in a sheet.
